items.title: Any agent anywhere: How to use Grafana Cloud with Claude, Cursor, and any other AI agent
items.summary: AI agents are becoming part of everyday engineering workflows, helping teams write code, troubleshoot issues, and automate tasks. But to be truly useful in production, these agents need access to more than code. They also need observability data and context to understand what's happening across your systems, investigate problems, and help you take action.At Grafana Labs, we believe that context should be available wherever you work. That’s one of the core ideas behind Grafana Cloud as the open agentic observability platform: the flexibility to work with your observability data through the AI agents you prefer—whether it’s Grafana Assistant, a coding agent in your IDE, or a tool you’ve built yourself—so you can investigate and troubleshoot issues without switching tools.In this post, we'll explore how to bring Grafana Cloud into your agentic workflows using tools like the Grafana Cloud MCP server and gcx, with practical examples along the way. You can also check out our ObservabilityCON 2026 talk in the video below to learn more.Three ways to use Grafana Cloud with AI agentsThere are multiple ways to bring Grafana Cloud observability data and context into your AI workflows, depending on where and how you prefer to work:Work directly in Grafana Cloud: Use Grafana Assistant, the AI-powered assistant built into Grafana Cloud, to investigate issues and interact with your observability data.Connect your preferred AI agent: Use the Grafana Cloud MCP server to bring Grafana Cloud data into compatible tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex.Work with coding agents and scripts: Use gcx, the Grafana Cloud command-line tool, to give coding agents access to observability data directly from their working environment.Whether you're working directly in Grafana Cloud with Grafana Assistant or using your own AI agents, you can choose the approach that works best for you. Let's look at how the Grafana Cloud MCP server and gcx make that possible outside of Grafana Cloud.Investigate an alert from your phone with Claude and Grafana Cloud MCP serverImagine you're waiting in line at a coffee shop when a Slack message arrives from your director of engineering. Something is wrong with the frontend, and they need your help.Your laptop is still in your backpack, but you don't necessarily need it to start investigating. With Claude connected to the Grafana Cloud MCP server, you can pull out your phone and ask a simple question: "Why is the frontend slow? Is there anything firing?"Claude can use Grafana Cloud data to answer your question directly in the conversation. In this example, it confirms that an alert is firing, shows a chart of the relevant signal, and identifies which pages are affected.You can then ask a follow-up question: how is this affecting the health of the frontend, and what's causing the problem? Again, Claude can return a visual Grafana Cloud view directly in the conversation, giving you more context about the health of your frontend application and helping you determine where to investigate next.All of this happens without leaving the conversation or opening your laptop. By the time you get your coffee, you've already confirmed the issue and started exploring its impact.How it works: The Grafana Cloud MCP server and MCP AppsThis experience is powered by two capabilities: the Grafana Cloud MCP server and MCP Apps.The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI agents to connect to external tools and data sources. The Grafana Cloud MCP server makes your Grafana Cloud observability data available to compatible agents, allowing them to query alerts, dashboards, and telemetry to help answer questions and investigate issues.That means you can interact with Grafana Cloud data from the AI tools you already use, rather than rely exclusively on the assistant built into your observability platform.MCP Apps take this a step further by bringing interactive Grafana Cloud views directly into your AI conversations. Instead of returning only a text description of an issue, an agent can display relevant visualizations, such as firing alerts and frontend health, alongside the conversation.These views are delivered by the Grafana Cloud MCP server and can appear in MCP clients that support them.To learn more, see the Grafana Cloud MCP server documentation. Continue your investigation in Cursor with Grafana Cloud context and gcxNow imagine you've grabbed your coffee and opened your laptop. You want to take a closer look at the frontend performance issue and get some help from your coding agent.You navigate to Grafana Cloud Frontend Observability, where a dashboard shows elevated time to first byte (TTFB), one of the symptoms of the slowdown.You could manually copy the relevant queries, filters, and time range into your coding agent and explain what you're looking at.
